title: “IT IS WRITTEN.”
paragraphs: “IT IS WRITTEN.”

Not shouted.
Not argued.
Not negotiated.
Just spoken.
And hell stepped back.

The desert was silent.
Forty days.
No bread.
No comfort.
No applause.
Only hunger.
And that’s when the devil came.

Because temptation rarely attacks when you’re strong.
It waits for the moment your body is weak…
your mind is tired…
your soul is lonely.
Then the whisper begins.

“If You are the Son of God… turn these stones into bread.”
— Gospel of Matthew 4:3
It sounded reasonable.
After all, Jesus was starving.
But the trap was deeper than hunger.

The enemy wasn’t just asking Jesus to eat.
He was tempting Him to act without trusting the Father.
To satisfy legitimate needs in illegitimate ways.
And Jesus answered with four words that shook the wilderness:
“IT IS WRITTEN.”

“Man shall not live by bread alone,
but by every word that comes from the mouth of God.”
— Deuteronomy 8:3
The devil tried again.
This time from the pinnacle of the temple.
“Throw Yourself down… the angels will catch You.”
A dare disguised as faith.
But Jesus saw through it.
Again the sword came out:
“IT IS WRITTEN.”

“You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.”
— Deuteronomy 6:16
The third attack was the boldest.
From a high mountain the devil showed Him all the kingdoms of the world.

Power.
Glory.
Authority.
One shortcut.
“All these I will give You… if You bow down and worship me.”

No cross.
No suffering.
No nails.
Just compromise.
And Jesus answered one final time:
“IT IS WRITTEN.”

“You shall worship the Lord your God and Him only shall you serve.”
— Deuteronomy 6:13
And the devil left.
Not because Jesus was louder.
But because truth carries authority that lies cannot survive.
Here is the Gospel hidden in that desert.

The first Adam faced temptation in a garden…
and he fell.

The second Adam—Jesus—faced temptation in a wilderness…
and He stood.

Where humanity failed,
Christ was faithful.
He resisted every temptation so He could become the spotless Savior who would later carry our sins to the cross.
Your victory over sin doesn’t start with your strength.
It starts with His obedience.

Because the One who said “It is written” in the wilderness
would later say “It is finished” on the cross.
And that changed everything.
Maybe today the enemy is whispering to you.

A secret sin.
A compromise.
A shortcut.
Remember the weapon Jesus used.

Not emotion.
Not willpower.
Scripture.
When lies come…
Speak truth.
When temptation rises…
Stand on the Word.
When darkness whispers…
Declare what heaven has already written.

Because the same Word that defeated the devil in the wilderness
is the Word that can guard your heart today.

And the Savior who resisted Satan
is the Savior who now lives to strengthen you.
So when temptation comes, say it with holy defiance:

IT.
IS.
WRITTEN.
Because some battles are won with fists…
But the greatest victories are won with the Word of God.
